description: Dot product: a weighted sum s = ∑ wᵢxᵢ, one multiply per pair and one running sum.

line_docs: The same sum with no index: W×X is every product at once, +/ adds them up, S receives the total.
m.purpose: Read right to left: W×X multiplies the two arrays entry by entry, +/ reduces the result with plus, and the total becomes S. No index appears: the notation says the whole sum at once. Placeholder glyphs.
m.title: The same sum in the proposed notation

line_docs: The sum: for each i from 1 to n, multiply w_i by x_i, and add all those products into s.
math.purpose: One line: the sum over i of the products of matching entries. The stacked limits say where i runs, from 1 to n; the subscripts say which entries are paired.
math.title: The sum as written on paper

name: dot-product

docs: The result: the sum of all the products, one number.
Definition: the left side is computed from the right side.
Add up every term: on paper a ∑ with its limits, in the notation a reduce by plus (+/), which needs no index.
The index: which pair of entries is being multiplied; it runs from 1 to n.
How many entries each array has; here 5.
The weights: one number per entry of the input.
The input: the entries the weights are paired with.
Multiply matching entries; written by juxtaposition on the Math face, as wᵢxᵢ, and as × in the notation.

title: Dot product

visual.purpose: The entries of w and x as cells, the current pair lit, their products in a row, and the running sum as a bar that grows one term per step.
visual.title: The two arrays, the products, and the sum growing
